title: Bottom-row collapse for the natural-index spectral-sequence abutment
statement: Let C be an abelian category and E a first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence indexed by natural bidegrees, starting at page two. Let H:N→C and assume E.AbutsTo H in the project convention: each H(n) has a decreasing subobject filtration with F^0=H(n), F^(n+1)=0, and quotient F^p/F^(p+1) isomorphic to E.pageInfinity(p,q) for p+q=n; this stable page is p+q+2. Assume every page-two term with q>0 is zero. Then H(n) is isomorphic to (E.page 2)^(n,0) for every n, including zero.

source.place: Original proof step 3: stationarity and collapse of the finite abutment filtration

proof.text: Induct on the page number minus two. The homology of a short complex with zero middle object is zero, and the successor-page isomorphism transports this vanishing. Hence every positive row vanishes on every page.

In bidegree (n,0) the differential of bidegree (r,1-r) has no outgoing target for r≥2. If an incoming arrow exists its source has positive second coordinate and is zero. Cycle inclusion and homology projection are therefore isomorphisms. Compose these with the successor-page comparison, inductively identifying page two with the stable page n+2.

For p<n, convergence and positive-row vanishing make the cokernel of the inclusion F^(p+1)→F^p zero. The inclusion is thus epic and monic, hence an isomorphism and the two subobjects equal. Induct from F^0=top to obtain F^n=top. Since F^(n+1)=bottom, the last quotient projection is an isomorphism. Compose the inverse top inclusion, this quotient projection, the graded-piece comparison and the inverse stationary-page comparison. This constructs the claimed isomorphism and is completely proved in Lean.
